summary:
Snapshot 2026-11-14 (ObesityWeek, Nov 14–17, has started). I checked 9 of these candidates with web searches. Here is what I found.

(1) The best early pick is a new Nature Metabolism paper from Nov 13. People who carry rare, damaging changes in the GLP-1 receptor gene lost about 2.4% of their body weight on semaglutide, against 8.9% in matched people without them. On tirzepatide, carriers lost 13.3% against 15.2%. Creators haven't picked it up yet. The BBC Science Focus piece "Why weight-loss drugs stop working" (Nov 14) points to the broad search question this answers: "tirzepatide not working".

(2) Stopping and keeping results is picking up again. The Cleveland Clinic newsroom piece is from Nov 14. Medscape, Fox and Medical Daily (a preprint) covered it on Nov 12–13. The real-world data we found online is the March Cleveland Clinic study of 7,938 adults, in which 45% kept their weight steady or kept losing after stopping. That fits Priority #2 on the playbook.

(3) The NAION eye warning (FDA, Nov 9) is at its peak in mainstream news, with The Hill, NeurologyLive and Blavity covering it on Nov 12–14. It is still worth one calm label-change explainer about which symptoms mean get help now.

(4) Two things from ObesityWeek to watch for a fast follow-up:
- The full REDEFINE 4 results. This is a randomized, open-label trial of CagriSema against tirzepatide in 809 adults: 23.0% vs 25.5%, and it missed non-inferiority. It counts for the 48-hour head-to-head L2 exception only if new full data comes out this week.
- New Phase 2 EloraTZP data in adults with type 2 diabetes: 23.3% at 48 weeks. That video was our biggest earner, but this result is not a head-to-head, so it's a Short or a pinned-comment update, not a long-form.

(5) Evergreen Lane A long-forms the playbook already favours: the first-month timeline, foods that ease side effects, and Foundayo what-to-expect. The China approval (Nov 12) has raised Foundayo searches.

(6) Thanksgiving fullness Shorts start Nov 18.

Rejected or caution:
- **Rejected:** microdosing (Scientific American) and the peptide or gray-market retatrutide craze.
- **Caution, Shorts only if at all:** case reports of psychiatric symptoms after stopping, the resurfaced pregnancy study, and the compounded-additive and black-market jab stories.

Other notes:
- I couldn't confirm the SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS 21.4% figure beyond Lilly's press release.
- The REDEFINE 9 Lancet D&E paper covers CagriSema against placebo only, so it isn't a head-to-head.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) not working? New Nature Metabolism genetics study (Nov 13): rare GLP1R gene variants blunted semaglutide weight loss (2.4% vs 8.9% in matched controls) but much less so with tirzepatide (13.3% vs 15.2%)
candidates.angle: Long-form: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Not Working? What Research Shows'. It answers the broad 'not working / non-responder' search: the range of responses in the trials, time on treatment, and what's been studied. The new genetics finding is the fresh hook. Frame it as 'linked to'. It's an observational genetic analysis, not a test you can order. Never suggest switching yourself. Bring response questions to your prescriber. Short (13:00): 'Why tirzepatide may work when semaglutide didn't, for a few people.'
keywords: why am I not losing weight on tirzepatide
candidates.why_now: Published Nov 13 in Nature Metabolism, with two companion papers. Bioengineer and Google News have picked it up, and BBC Science Focus ran 'Why weight-loss drugs stop working' on Nov 14, but it isn't in mainstream health news yet and there are almost no creator videos. It attaches to the evergreen 'not working' search demand, which is broad, so it's Lane A-eligible.

evidence.signal: Rare damaging GLP1R variants: 2.4% vs 8.9% weight loss on semaglutide; 13.3% vs 15.2% on tirzepatide
Rare GLP1R variants diminish semaglutide but not tirzepatide effect
Earlier common-variant study: GLP1R and GIPR variants linked to weight loss and nausea on tirzepatide

candidates.topic: Keeping results after stopping tirzepatide: SURMOUNT-4 (335 vs 335; +14.0% regain on placebo, still 9.9% below baseline) plus Cleveland Clinic real-world data (Nov 14 newsroom piece; 7,938 adults, 45% held or kept losing after stopping)
candidates.angle: Broad Lane A: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) After Stopping: What Trials Show'. Keep to trial and cohort evidence only: regain varies, and ongoing care was linked to holding on. Never give stopping advice; the decision is made with a prescriber. Must be distinct from our Stopping video (11-04): this one is about maintenance after stopping. Otherwise ship it as a chapter or Short and send Stopping viewers to it.
keywords: what happens when you stop mounjaro
how to keep weight off after ozempic
candidates.why_now: The Cleveland Clinic newsroom piece came out Nov 14 alongside ObesityWeek. Medscape (Nov 13), Fox News (Nov 12) and Medical Daily (Nov 13, preprint) cover regain. Our Stopping video is our best recent broad video (6.35% CTR).

evidence.signal: Study on the best strategies after stopping GLP-1 medicines
Real-world: modest regain after stopping; 45% maintained or kept losing
Can patients stop GLP-1s without regaining weight?

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) eye warning explained: FDA class-wide NAION label change (Nov 9). About 6.4 NAION cases per 100,000 person-years on GLP-1 medicines in the FDA's 126-trial review; it's rare, and sudden painless vision loss means urgent care
candidates.angle: A label-change explainer, which the owner lists as a search-demand format: what NAION is, how rare it is, the exact label language, which symptoms mean 'get help right away', and who to tell about existing eye conditions. Calm, never fear-led. Includes the scoped don't-stop line.
candidates.why_now: Opinion and follow-up coverage keeps coming: The Hill on Nov 12, NeurologyLive on Nov 13, Blavity and Demócrata on Nov 14. Search demand is at its peak. Our edge is quoting the label exactly with the absolute rate.

evidence.signal: FDA requires class-wide GLP-1 RA labeling change for potential NAION risk
NAION warning added to Warnings and Precautions across the class
126 trials, >134,000 patients reviewed

candidates.topic: Did CagriSema beat tirzepatide? Full REDEFINE 4 results at ObesityWeek (randomized, open-label, 84 weeks, 809 adults with obesity plus at least one comorbidity: 23.0% vs 25.5%; 20.2% vs 23.6% treatment-regimen estimand; non-inferiority not met)
candidates.angle: Use the fast-turn head-to-head L2 exception only if full or new data (a publication or a presentation with side effects and dropouts) goes public at ObesityWeek this week. Otherwise make a 13:00 tirzepatide-first Short. Report both arms and both estimands, and say plainly that it was open-label. CagriSema isn't approved.
candidates.why_now: ObesityWeek runs Nov 14–17. Novo is presenting CagriSema data (REDEFINE 9 is already out). Full REDEFINE 4 detail would be the only randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide this week, and that's the EloraTZP model that earned 44% of our watch time.

evidence.signal: CagriSema fails primary endpoint vs tirzepatide
23% vs 25.5%, 809 adults, non-inferiority missed
Novo presenting CagriSema and Wegovy data at ObesityWeek 2026

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) first month: what to expect, from the label and trials only (appetite and food noise, GI effects that happened mostly during dose escalation and decreased over time, injection-site reactions, when to call)
candidates.angle: Priority #1 broad Lane A, in the what-to-expect timeline format. A 'you' scenario opener, a second payoff at 15–30 s, and no dosing or titration amounts. Link it to Side Effects and How Long.
candidates.predicted_peak: evergreen; New Year starters push demand from late Dec
candidates.why_now: New starters are steady, and the New Year starter wave is about 6 weeks out. How Long added +31 minutes today. CNN's 'Doctors explain GLP-1 side effects' (Nov 13) shows the side-effect question is current.

evidence.signal: Doctors explain GLP-1 side effects
GI adverse reactions mostly during dose escalation, decreasing over time

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: full after 3 bites, protein first, smaller plates, eating slowly, easing nausea at a big holiday meal
candidates.angle: 20:00 funnel Shorts from Nov 18, pointing to the Thanksgiving long-form. A felt-moment hook ('Full after three bites on tirzepatide? Here's why.'). The label says stomach emptying is slower; never present that as the cause.
keywords: full after a few bites zepbound
candidates.why_now: Seen in 8 snapshots. The holiday search window opens on Nov 18, and our best Reel (428) was this topic.

evidence.signal: 'Full after 3 bites' Reel got 428 views, our best; Shorts posted too early only got 21–24
Delayed gastric emptying; GI adverse reactions

candidates.topic: EloraTZP (eloralintide + tirzepatide) new Phase 2 data at ObesityWeek: adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes, 23.3% average weight loss at 48 weeks, A1C down 2.9 points
candidates.angle: Our biggest earner's follow-up. A 13:00 'what's confirmed' Short with the population named (type 2 diabetes, Phase 2, investigational, not approved), and a pinned comment or description update on the EloraTZP video. It isn't a head-to-head, so no long-form (pipeline explainer ban), unless the abstract shows a randomized tirzepatide-alone arm, which would qualify.
candidates.why_now: Lilly's ObesityWeek press release is from Nov 14. 'eloralintide' and 'eloratzp' are our proven search terms (230 and 88 searches).

evidence.signal: New data across Zepbound, Foundayo, EloraTZP and retatrutide at ObesityWeek
EloraTZP Phase 2: 54.1 lb (23.3%) at 48 weeks

candidates.topic: Retatrutide Phase 3 at ObesityWeek: TRIUMPH-1 sleep apnea (AHI down an average of 36.1 events per hour, 60.6%, at 80 weeks) and knee OA pain (WOMAC down 73.1% TRIUMPH-1, 75.8% TRIUMPH-4)
candidates.angle: A 13:00 'new retatrutide Phase 3 data, what's confirmed?' Short: populations, the timeframe, 'investigational, isn't approved', and more serious adverse events than placebo. Never link to sellers. The Rogan and peptide hype is exactly why a calm, sourced version matters.
candidates.why_now: New sleep apnea data on Nov 14, plus knee results seen in 4 earlier snapshots. Rogan comments on Nov 13 are pushing gray-market interest.

evidence.signal: Retatrutide sleep apnea and knee pain results at ObesityWeek
Lilly presents obesity trial results at ObesityWeek 2026

candidates.topic: Foods that ease tirzepatide side effects: nausea, burping and heartburn, constipation (smaller meals, eating slowly, stopping when full, less greasy food, fluids, fibre)
candidates.angle: Priority #3 broad Lane A: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Side Effects: Foods That Help'. It covers the felt-symptom searches (nausea, burping, heartburn) inside one broad video with chapters. Use the label's tips plus NHS advice, and cite the label for the urgent signs.
keywords: what to eat on mounjaro for nausea
candidates.why_now: Burping/heartburn and nausea have appeared in 4 and 3 snapshots. Holiday meals are coming, and per the analytics broad topics beat narrow ones.

evidence.signal: Nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting, constipation, dyspepsia, eructation listed
Doctors explain GLP-1 side effects

candidates.topic: Foundayo (orforglipron) what to expect, label only, as China approves it (Nov 12) and the sleep apnea Phase 3 (ATTAIN-OSA, JAMA Nov 9) adds interest
candidates.angle: Priority #4 Lane A: 'Foundayo (Orforglipron): What to Expect' covers taking it, common side effects, label trial results (top label dose −11.1% in Trial 1) and when to call. Sleep apnea isn't an approved use, so say it 'isn't approved' for that.
candidates.why_now: There was a wave of China approval coverage (Nov 12–13), and the Wegovy pill real-world 6% data came out at ObesityWeek. Foundayo earned 336 minutes for us, and it's an approved drug with search demand.

evidence.signal: Lilly first with a GLP-1 weight-loss pill approved in China
Has Foundayo found its niche in sleep apnoea?

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide injection site reactions: redness, itching, small lumps (label 6–8% by dose vs about 2% placebo) and when to call your prescriber
candidates.angle: An 08:00 'Is this normal?' visible-body Short. It's our second-best Short type, with 243 and 200 views. A new fact each time: rotation per the IFU, and what the label counts as a reaction. Pair it with a device how-to chapter.
candidates.why_now: It has appeared in 6 snapshots across 2 variants. Visible-body worries are the proven Shorts winner.

evidence.signal: Injection site reactions 6–8% vs about 2% placebo
Injection-site Shorts got 243 and 200 views against a 64-view median

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: will it grow back? (label 5.4% vs 0.9%; women 7.1%, men 0.5%)
candidates.angle: The one hair Short allowed this week, only after the Hair long-form is verified clean. A new angle that isn't growth or prevalence: what the label says about timing alongside rapid weight loss, and when to see a doctor. The Studio related-video link goes to the Hair long-form.
keywords: will hair grow back after mounjaro
candidates.why_now: Our biggest Short ever (1,025 views). The hair-in-women Short had 112 views on day 1 on 11-13.

evidence.signal: Hair loss 5.4% vs 0.9%; more in women

candidates.topic: Lifting weights on tirzepatide: T-REx RCT (Nature Medicine, Nov 9). In men and postmenopausal women aged 50–70, resistance training linked to about 25% less lean-mass loss, and strength up about 10% vs down about 10% without training
candidates.angle: A 20:00 funnel Short pointing to the Strength long-form, with the population named. The Lancet COURAGE trial (Nov 11, muscle-sparing antibodies with semaglutide) is background only; it's investigational.
candidates.why_now: News-Medical (Nov 12), MindBodyGreen (Nov 12) and Korean press (Nov 14) are still spreading it. Strength is still earning (+15 minutes).

evidence.signal: Resistance exercise to attenuate lean mass loss during tirzepatide: RCT
Trevogrumab ± garetosmab for muscle preservation with semaglutide (Phase 2)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and alcohol at holiday parties: what the label says, why a drink may feel different, and the low-blood-sugar caveat for people on insulin or sulfonylureas
candidates.angle: A holiday-party Short from Nov 18 pointing to the Alcohol long-form (11-12). Never a 'safe amount'. The Neuropharmacology rodent study (Nov 12) is animal data only, so don't use it as a hook.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 5 snapshots, and holiday-party season is starting. The long-form already exists, so this sends viewers to it.

evidence.signal: Hypoglycemia risk with insulin or sulfonylureas
Systematic review: incretin therapies for alcohol use disorder

candidates.topic: Zepbound (tirzepatide) in teens: SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS at ObesityWeek (Lilly reports 21.4% average BMI reduction at 72 weeks in ages 12–17 with obesity)
candidates.angle: Possible 13:00 Short for parents: what the trial showed, that adolescent use isn't approved in the US for weight (check the current label), and to talk to a paediatric clinician. Hold it until the abstract or a publication confirms the numbers.
candidates.why_now: Lilly's ObesityWeek release (Nov 14), plus ABC News on a teen on a GLP-1 (Nov 13) and The Guardian on children in England (Nov 14). The audience fit is secondary (parents).

evidence.signal: Lilly brings Zepbound teen data to ObesityWeek
Hundreds of children in England prescribed weight-loss jabs

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and heart failure: AHA 2026 biomarker data in obesity-related HFpEF (building on SUMMIT), plus semaglutide HFpEF MRI substudies in Nature Medicine
candidates.angle: A benefits-beyond-weight Short, scoped to adults with HFpEF and obesity. Only state what the trial measured (biomarkers, structure), not outcomes it didn't test.
candidates.why_now: Clinical Trials Arena (Nov 13) and two Nature Medicine HFpEF papers (Nov 8). It isn't in consumer media yet, but its search demand is narrow.

evidence.source: Clinical Trials Arena via Google News (Nov 13)
evidence.signal: Tirzepatide improves key biomarkers in obesity-related heart failure
Semaglutide hemodynamics in HFpEF with obesity, RCT

candidates.topic: Psychiatric symptoms after stopping tirzepatide: 2 case reports (Prim Care Companion CNS Disord) amplified by NY Post and others (Nov 11–12)
candidates.angle: Not a standalone piece. At most one careful sentence in the Stopping and keeping-results script: 'two case reports; cause not established; tell your prescriber about mood changes'. Standalone coverage would be fear bait built on n=2.
candidates.why_now: Tabloid pickup on Nov 11–12, but the evidence is weak (case reports).

evidence.signal: Reports of psychosis after stopping GLP-1s
Mounjaro/Zepbound changes after stopping

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines around pregnancy: the 750,000-pregnancy study (Human Reproduction Open) resurfacing in ScienceDaily (Nov 13): no preterm-birth link when used for weight, higher risk in people with pre-existing diabetes
candidates.angle: Low priority. It's observational, and our Birth Control video earned 7 minutes. If used at all, add one line to existing pregnancy-planning content citing the label, with no reassurance that the medicines are 'safe in pregnancy'.
candidates.why_now: A ScienceDaily repost on Nov 13. The original is from spring 2026, so it isn't new.

evidence.signal: Study of 750,000 pregnancies
Key caveats of the study

candidates.topic: Black-market and compounded GLP-1 warnings: BBC 'I'm lucky to be alive' (Nov 14) and the University of Utah study on untested additive combinations in compounded GLP-1s (Nov 13)
candidates.angle: At most 1 gray-market Short a week: 'Why the source of your tirzepatide matters'. Point only to prescription channels and talking to a prescriber, and never name sellers or prices. Skip it if a gray-market Short has already run this week.
candidates.why_now: BBC and University of Utah coverage on Nov 13–14. UK audience fit.

evidence.signal: Woman's warning over black-market weight-loss jabs
GLP-1s often contain untested additive combinations

candidates.topic: REJECT: GLP-1 microdosing for longevity (Scientific American, Nov 12), the 'peptide craze' and Rogan retatrutide hype, plus GLP-1 pricing, CVS $350, Deloitte coverage and Medicare stories
candidates.angle: Don't produce. Microdosing and self-titration are on the never-cover list. Pipeline gray-market hype risks promoting research-chemical sources. Cost and coverage are banned angles.
candidates.why_now: There's a lot of traffic, but it falls outside the brand's guardrails.

evidence.signal: Could microdosing GLP-1 drugs boost longevity?
Rogan says retatrutide could beat GLP-1 drugs as peptide market faces a purity test
